findings.description: The EBS data volume does not set encrypted = true or a KMS key, so its contents may be stored unencrypted unless an external account-level default happens to enforce encryption.

The instance user-data contains a static AWS access key ID and secret access key. User data is retrievable by principals with instance access/describe permissions and the credentials are exposed in IaC source, enabling unauthorized AWS access if valid.
No metadata_options block requires IMDSv2, so the instance can permit IMDSv1. An SSRF flaw on the web server could then be used to retrieve instance metadata and any attached role credentials.
TCP port 22 is open to 0.0.0.0/0, exposing remote administration to the entire internet and enabling scanning and password/key attack attempts.
The security group permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0. This provides an unrestricted path for data exfiltration or command-and-control traffic from a compromised instance.
The bucket used to archive VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration. Archived network metadata is therefore not explicitly protected at rest.
The backup snapshot is created from an EBS volume that is not configured for encryption, so the snapshot is not explicitly protected with encryption at rest.
